threads.head: In-Store Visits Driven
threads.finding: Store visit intent was the second-largest intent class, with 210 attributed visits (22.11% share), and the Store Locator page was reached by 210 visitors -- consistent with active in-store consideration among exposed audiences.
threads.meaning: A meaningful share of attributed visitors demonstrated direct store-seeking behavior after exposure, signaling that the campaign is moving audiences through the lower funnel toward physical visits.
threads.action: Consider extending flight weight in Washington, DC -- the top market by attributed rate -- to sustain in-store visit momentum heading into the next campaign period.

threads.head: Brand Awareness Reached Scale
threads.finding: Product consideration was the single largest intent class at 480 visits and a 50.53% share of attributed sessions, with an additional 190 visits (20% share) landing on the Homepage.
threads.meaning: More than half of all attributed visits reflect upper-funnel brand engagement -- audiences are actively exploring the brand and its offerings after seeing the ad, a strong awareness signal.

threads.head: Research Intent Adds Depth
threads.finding: Research and learning pages drew 45 attributed visits (4.74% share), with the Kitchen Remodel page alone reached by 300 visitors (32% of top-page traffic).
threads.meaning: Content-driven engagement on category pages like Kitchen Remodel shows the campaign is generating not just awareness impressions but genuine product interest -- audiences are going deeper than the homepage.
threads.action: Amplifying creative messaging tied to high-interest categories such as kitchen remodeling could deepen this research engagement in future flights.

threads.head: Washington, DC Leads Markets
threads.finding: Washington, DC delivered an attributed rate of 1.69% against Richmond's 1.515%, with zip code 20852 (Washington, DC) outperforming the campaign baseline at 1.47x and zip 23225 (Richmond) at 1.17x.
threads.meaning: Both markets produced outperforming zip codes, but Washington, DC showed stronger response across both market-level rate and its leading zip -- the mid-flight budget shift toward the stronger market appears to have been well-placed.
threads.action: Prioritizing Washington, DC and specifically zip 20852 in future planning would concentrate spend where response rates are highest.

goal_alignment_notes: Read goal priority as: 1) Drive in-store visits -- stated first and most operationally specific, representing the lower-funnel conversion outcome the campaign is built around; 2) Increase brand awareness -- a supporting goal that the upper-funnel intent data (product consideration, homepage, research visits) speaks to directly.

This is consistent with the computed facts showing Washington, DC outperforming Richmond at the market level and both outperformer zips present in the data.
